title: We Gave an Agent Production Code Access and Then Tried to Sleep at Night — Moritz Johner, Form3
talk_summary: Form3 built 'Patch Pilot', a two-layer system where a deterministic Go controller does discovery, git/PR/CI actions, and credential-holding, while LLM agents only edit files in a cloned repo and reason about CI failures. Infosec review forced them to split credentials, sandbox agents in Firecracker microVMs with per-layer network policy, and add prompt-injection evals.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic controller holds dangerous credentials; agents only touch files
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent edits files on disk only; the deterministic Go layer does commit, push, PR creation, CI triggering, and CI log download, so prompt injection cannot reach GitHub write or CI-trigger credentials.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It doesn't commit, it doesn't push, it doesn't create a PR, it doesn't watch the CI itself. It just modifies files on the file system.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic vetting of agent output before commit
takeaways.what_they_do: After each agent invocation the controller checks the diff for nonsense (empty files, compiled binaries left in repo) before committing and opening a PR.

Every agent invocation ends with a short structured retrospective (what went well, what went wrong, missing tools, missing context); these are aggregated across PRs to find infra vs. repo-complexity issues and then fix system prompts or add repo-specific instructions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at the end of every agent invocation, we ask the agent to do a very short and simple retrospective. What went well, what went wrong, what tools are missing

takeaways.technique: MicroVM isolation instead of Docker-socket sandbox
takeaways.what_they_do: They abandoned giving agents a host Docker socket (privileged-container escape = game over) and moved to Firecracker microVMs with their own kernel, plus a vsock-based network forwarder applying per-layer egress policy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you give it that Docker socket. At that point, it's more or less game over for you

takeaways.what_they_do: They built a crafted test repository containing deprecated functions and migration guides that try to recruit the agent into malicious actions, and run Patch Pilot against it to verify it isn't hijacked.
Agents are told to make the smallest effective change tied to the finding (not bump to latest) and, on CI-failure retries, explicitly told not to revert their previous changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: LLMs kind of tend to just revert the previous changes that it did. So, we got to tell it to not do this.
